title: Boréale · Homebrew for the long nights
description: Open-source homebrew for the Nintendo Switch: PlayGuard, parental controls on the console; PlayShelf, your game library on the console; Aurore, the interface library behind both.
hero_lede: Open-source apps for the Nintendo Switch, made with care and one shared look. Parental controls on the console, your own game library, and the interface library behind both.
projects_lede: Each one has its own site, its documentation and a simulator or a demo you can try in your browser.
playguard_text: Nintendo's parental controls, right on the console. No phone app, no Nintendo account, no internet.
playshelf_text: Your game library, on the console. Browse a library server you run yourself and install your own backups and homebrew.
aurore_text: A Switch-like interface for your app, on every screen. The borealis fork that PlayGuard and PlayShelf are built with.
ground_1_text: Cadran, Aurore's look: an icon rail, cards, vector icons, light and dark themes. Learn one app, you know the other.
ground_2_text: Fifteen languages, switched while the app runs. PlayGuard's guide is in all fifteen, PlayShelf's in English and French.
ground_3_text: PlayGuard and PlayShelf run in your browser, on a simulated console, before anything touches your SD card.
ground_4_text: GPLv3, built and tested on GitHub at each change, with the code, the issues and the roadmap in public.
promise_text: These apps run on a console with custom firmware, at your own risk. They work with what you own: none of them supports, or will support, a service that distributes games without the rights to do so.
footer_nintendo: Not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. Nintendo Switch is a trademark of Nintendo.
lost_text: This page does not exist, or not any more. The projects are on the home page.
feed_subtitle: The releases of PlayGuard, PlayShelf and Aurore.
playguard_shot: PlayGuard's Today screen: 40 minutes of play left, the bedtime alarm at 21:00 and the state of the parental controls.
playshelf_shot: PlayShelf's catalogue: made-up games from a demo server, ready to install.
aurore_shot: Aurore's demo, its Welcome tab: Aurore's name over an aurora, the systems it runs on and a dashboard of three cards.
atlas_text: Open data on the games of every platform, from the Switch to Steam, GOG and the Xbox, and the links between a game's ids from one store to the next. Plain JSON files, rebuilt every week. PlayShelf reads the Switch's.
lantern_text: An open, versioned REST and JSON protocol between console homebrews and the library servers people run at home for their own games: browse, download with SHA-256 checks, keep save backups and cheats. It comes with JSON Schemas, a conformance suite and a reference server. The specification under CC BY 4.0, the rest under MIT.
legal_lede: What this site learns about you, and who is behind it.
legal_translation: This page is a translation; where they differ, the French version prevails.
privacy_1: This site sets no cookie, and keeps nothing in your browser but the language you choose in its header. It loads nothing from another site: its fonts, images and scripts are served with it.
privacy_2: It counts its visits with Umami Cloud, in the European Union (Frankfurt), without cookie. For each page seen: the page, the page you came from, your browser, system and kind of device, your screen's size, your language and your country. Your IP address is used to tell your country and to tell visits apart, and is not kept with them. The counts are kept six months, used only to know what is read, and never sold or shared. Umami's policy: umami.is/privacy.
privacy_3: The projects' sites (guard, shelf and aurore.boreale.dev) are counted the same way; their simulators and demo are not. GitHub, which serves all of them, records its visitors' IP addresses for its servers' security (GitHub's privacy statement).
privacy_4: For a question about your data, or to have it erased: an issue on GitHub. You may also complain to your data protection authority; in France, the CNIL.
notice_publisher_text: JigSawFr, a non-professional publisher, whose identity is held by the host, as French law (LCEN) allows.
notice_contact_text: An issue on GitHub; a security flaw, privately on GitHub.
notice_rights_text: The site's code is free software under the GPLv3 (its repository); the names Boréale, PlayGuard, PlayShelf and Aurore, and their marks, are reserved. Nintendo Switch is a trademark of Nintendo.
insights_moved: PlayInsights is now Atlas, with a site of its own: a map of every game on every platform, its files, and an explorer to browse them game by game.
support_lede: Every app here is free, all of it, and stays so. A donation pays for what code cannot: the consoles to test it on.
support_sponsors: Monthly or once, from your GitHub account. Monthly support is what keeps the testing going from one device to the next.
support_kofi: Once, with or without an account. Each Ko-fi goal is one device: once it is reached, the device is bought.
support_hardware_lede: Aurore, and the apps built with it, run on more systems than there are here to try them on, and what never runs on the real thing only hopefully works. What is missing, in the order it is wanted:
hw_3ds: For Aurore's port to the 3DS, its reference console: nothing has run on one yet.
hw_android_name: An Android phone with a notch
hw_android: For the screen's cut-outs and edges, on Android 9 and later.
hw_vita: One of Aurore's systems, never yet tried on the console.
hw_ps4: The same, on a firmware that runs homebrew.
hw_appletv: Aurore's tvOS build, never yet tried.
hw_mac: macOS, today tested only by the build servers.
support_owned: Already here: a Switch, an iPhone, a PC and an Xbox Series X.
support_promise_title: What a donation is, and is not
support_promise_1: A gift, not a purchase: it unlocks no feature, no support and no early build; everyone already has them all. Your name in the thanks, if you want it, is all it brings.
support_promise_2: When a device is bought, this page says so, and again once the apps are tested on it. What is left over goes to the next one.
support_privacy: GitHub or Ko-fi takes the payment. What they pass on, and what is done with it: privacy.
privacy_5: A donation, through GitHub Sponsors or Ko-fi, is paid to them, under their own policies. JigSawFr receives from them only your username and what you choose to share with it (a name, an email address, a message); it is used only to thank you, your name is shown in the thanks only if you agree, and none of it is sold or shared.
home_support_text: Everything here is free. Donations buy the hardware the apps still need testing on, a New 2DS XL first.
how_lede: Boréale is one person: JigSawFr, a full-stack engineer who has built and run production software for years. AI coding assistants are part of the workshop, like the compiler, the tests and the CI. They write fast; I decide what ships.
how_me_1: The architecture, the scope, what ships and what doesn't
how_me_2: Reviewing every change before it reaches main
how_me_3: Testing on a real console when a change touches it
how_me_4: Signing every commit and every release
how_ai_1: First drafts of code and tests, which I rework
how_ai_3: The translations into 15 languages, checked as far as I can
how_ai_4: Reviews on top of mine, never instead of them
how_reviewed: No change reaches main without being read and passing CI.
how_noai: AI helps write the code. The homebrews call no AI service and send it nothing. The Home Assistant integration can offer its actions to Home Assistant's own assistant, if you expose a console to it.
how_lang: Open an issue: it is fixed in the next version.
brand_lede: Boréale and its projects share one look: a frame in the aurora's colours around the night, one drawing in snow inside. This page sums it up, with the files to use it.
brand_mark_text: It always stands on the night's blue, with room around it of at least a quarter of its width. One gradient, aurora green at the top left to violet at the bottom right, never reversed. Under 24 px, use the small mark; to print or engrave in one ink, the white or black one.
brand_colours_text: The night takes the room and the aurora comes in touches: about 60 % abyss, 20 % night, 12 % snow, 6 % aurora.
brand_contrast: Snow, mist, aurora and ice all pass WCAG AAA on the night. Violet does not: keep it for large text and graphics, never a paragraph.
brand_type_text: Sora for names and headings, Figtree for running text, JetBrains Mono for addresses, commands and versions. All three are under the SIL Open Font License and served with the site.
brand_files_text: The mark, the name and the tokens (colours, gradient, fonts) the projects read. Every project's icons and banners are in the full kit.
home_brand_text: The apps, the integration and the sites share a mark, a palette and three fonts. Here they are.
